description.narrative: AGG will fund decarbonization efforts in various sectors including (i) housing, (ii) e-mobility, (iii) manufacturing or industrial facilities, and (iv) energy efficiency appliances, such as clean cooking solutions. Furthermore, IFC expects the Fund to attract additional investment to these sectors by demonstrating the viability of green investments in Sub-Saharan Africa. With new entrants in the market, IFC expects the Fund to foster a deeper integration of target countries firms to global financial markets.

Africa Go Green (AGG or the Fund) is a dedicated pan-African greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction debt fund, established by KFW with the support from the German Government (BMZ). AGG primarily focuses on Energy Efficiency (EE) and Renewable Energy (RE) opportunities, with a prioritization on West African countries. AGG is raising up to US$250 million capital comprised of debt, senior equity and junior equity. AGG will provide medium to long-term debt, mezzanine financing, and guarantees as well as technical assistance (TA) for green housing, green appliances, industrial energy efficiency and green mobility sectors.
